summary:
A Reuters-sourced news item republished by Allwork.Space reports that more than 100 companies, including OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft, Alphabet, Amazon, Broadcom, Capital One, Cloudflare, CrowdStrike, General Motors, IBM, Mastercard, Oracle, Robinhood, Shopify and Visa, signed a joint letter issued Thursday calling for a society-wide defensive surge against an anticipated wave of AI-driven cyberattacks.

Key points:
- The letter argues there is only a limited window of time to make the digital world much more secure before AI-enabled attack capability becomes widespread, saying such attacks will become far more common in the coming months as models globally grow more capable.
- It urges government and industry leaders to commit their full technology, resources and expertise, asks governments to expedite trusted access programs (which grant selected companies early access to more powerful models before general release), and asks all other organizations to treat cyber defense as an immediate leadership priority.
- CISA and the White House did not immediately respond to a request for comment. The article notes the Trump administration imposed deep cuts on CISA, with agency staffing falling roughly a third last year.
- The piece frames the warning as already materializing, citing rogue actors increasingly using large language models to break into organizations worldwide.
- In June, the Five Eyes intelligence alliance (U.S., Britain, Canada, Australia, New Zealand) issued a rare joint statement warning that the AI revolution was poised to fundamentally transform cybersecurity.

Reporting credited to Raphael Satter, edited by Chizu Nomiyama and Lisa Shumaker. The item contains no workplace-specific operational detail: no coverage of visitor management, desk or room booking, hybrid policy, attendance tooling or facilities operations. Relevance to workplace technology is indirect, via enterprise security posture and the governance of AI model access.
